name: HeatLens – Heatmap & Click Tracking Analytics
author: hcandnmz

sections.description:
HeatLens Analytics is a free, self-hosted heatmap plugin for WordPress. It turns invisible visitor behavior into visual, actionable insights: see exactly where users click, tap, scroll, and hesitate — then get data-driven recommendations to improve conversions.

Unlike bloated SaaS analytics tools, HeatLens Analytics runs entirely on your WordPress server. No external tracking, no monthly fees, no data leaving your site.

🔥 Heatmap Visualization

See click density overlaid on your actual pages. Filter by device type (desktop, tablet, mobile), date range, and event type. Compare two time periods side by side with the built-in comparison mode.

🖱️ Complete Click & Touch Tracking

  • Precise X/Y coordinates with element identification (tag, ID, class, text)
  • Separate desktop mouse clicks and mobile/tablet touch events
  • Screen resolution and viewport tracking
  • Automatic device type detection

⚡ Rage Click & Dead Click Detection

Automatically identifies two critical UX problems:

  • Rage Clicks — 3+ clicks within 2 seconds in a 50×50px area means frustration
  • Dead Clicks — Clicks on non-interactive elements that produce no response

These are the areas losing you conversions right now.

📊 Scroll Depth Analytics

Uses IntersectionObserver API to accurately track how far visitors scroll (25%, 50%, 75%, 100%). Know if your most important content is actually being seen.

💡 Smart Suggestions Engine

5 analysis algorithms run automatically every 6 hours:

  1. Heat Density Grid — Finds click hotspots and suggests CTA placement
  2. CTA Performance — Identifies underperforming call-to-action buttons
  3. Scroll Depth Analysis — Detects important content buried below the fold
  4. Rage/Dead Click Areas — Flags frustration zones for immediate fixing
  5. WooCommerce Conversion — Tracks add-to-cart click-through rates

Each suggestion includes a confidence score so you can prioritize.

🛒 WooCommerce Integration

When WooCommerce is active, HeatLens Analytics provides additional analytics:

  • Add-to-cart button click tracking
  • Proceed-to-checkout and place-order button clicks
  • Add-to-cart rate across product pages
  • Rage clicks on the cart and checkout pages

📤 Export Reports

  • CSV — Works everywhere
  • XLSX — Real Excel files with a styled header row, frozen header and auto-filter. Built in, no extra libraries needed
  • PDF — Optional, for developers: available when the TCPDF library is installed via Composer

🛡️ Privacy First — Built for GDPR & KVKK

  • No IP addresses stored — ever
  • No cookies — anonymous localStorage session IDs
  • Consent integration — in the optional GDPR mode nothing is tracked or stored until the visitor consents. Works with page caching and supports the WP Consent API, Complianz, CookieYes, Cookiebot and GDPR Cookie Consent
  • No form values — text typed into inputs is never recorded; only the visible label of clicked buttons, links and headings is stored
  • WordPress Privacy Tools — data export and erasure support
  • Ready-made privacy policy text — auto-appends to your privacy page

🚀 Performance

  • Vanilla JavaScript, zero dependencies, under 8KB gzipped
  • Async/defer script loading — zero render blocking
  • Batch event sending (every 15 seconds or 20 events) with Beacon API
  • Built-in bot filtering (Googlebot, Bingbot, etc.) and rate limiting (60 requests per minute per IP)
  • Throttled to max 10 events per second and 300 events per page view
sections.installation:
1. Upload the heatlens-analytics folder to /wp-content/plugins/
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress
  3. You’ll be redirected to the Welcome page, where you can generate demo data with one click to explore the features
  4. Go to HeatLens Analytics → Settings to configure tracking options
  5. (Optional, developers) For PDF export, run composer install --no-dev in the plugin directory

Minimum Requirements

  • WordPress 5.8 or higher
  • PHP 7.4 or higher
  • MySQL 5.6 or MariaDB 10.0
sections.faq:
What does a heatmap plugin show me?

A heatmap plugin draws a colour overlay on your own pages: red where visitors click the most, green where they click the least. With HeatLens you also see how far people scroll, which elements they click in frustration (rage clicks) and which ones they expect to be clickable but are not (dead clicks). Together this tells you where a call-to-action works and where visitors get stuck.

Does this plugin slow down my website?

The tracking script is under 8KB gzipped, loads asynchronously in the footer, and sends events in batches to minimize network requests, so the impact on page load speed is minimal.

Is this GDPR / KVKK compliant?

HeatLens Analytics is designed to help you comply: it never stores IP addresses, uses anonymous session IDs (localStorage, not cookies), keeps all data on your own server, and has an optional GDPR mode in which nothing is tracked or stored until a consent plugin such as Complianz, CookieYes or Cookiebot reports consent. It also supports WordPress Privacy Tools. Whether your site as a whole is compliant depends on your own setup and local law, so enable GDPR mode if consent is required in your jurisdiction.

How long until I get suggestions?

By default, the analysis engine waits for at least 100 unique sessions over 48 hours before generating suggestions. These thresholds are configurable in Settings → Analysis.

Does it work with WooCommerce?

Yes. When WooCommerce is active, HeatLens Analytics recognises clicks on add-to-cart, proceed-to-checkout and place-order buttons (classic and block themes) and shows product page views, the add-to-cart rate, checkout clicks and rage clicks on the cart and checkout pages in the dashboard.

Can I track only specific pages?

Yes. Go to Settings → General and set URL patterns. Use * for all pages, or enter specific paths like /pricing/* or /products/* — one pattern per line. Wildcards are supported.

Does it work with page builders like Elementor?

Yes. HeatLens Analytics uses event delegation at the document level, so it captures clicks on any element regardless of how the page was built.

How do I export my data?

Go to the Page Analysis page, apply your filters (page, date range, device type), then click the CSV or XLSX export button. PDF export appears when the optional TCPDF library is installed.

Is this an alternative to Hotjar or Microsoft Clarity?

It covers the core of what those services are used for — click heatmaps, scroll depth, rage click and dead click detection — but runs entirely inside your WordPress site. Nothing is sent to an external service, there are no page-view limits and no account is needed. It does not include session recordings.

Where is the data stored?

In three custom tables in your own WordPress database. Data older than the retention period you choose (90 days by default) is deleted automatically, and everything is removed when you uninstall the plugin.

Is it compatible with caching plugins?

Yes. Events are sent to the WordPress REST API, which page caching does not affect, and the tracker configuration contains nothing user-specific, so cached pages work normally. When you activate the plugin or change a tracking setting, HeatLens asks the common caching plugins (WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache and others) to clear their page cache so the change takes effect right away. If you use a different cache or a CDN, clear it once after activation.
sections.changelog:
1.1.1

  • New: a one-time, dismissible review reminder on the HeatLens screens, shown to administrators only after two weeks of use and 50 recorded sessions

1.1.0

  • New: clicks are stored relative to the element they hit, so the heatmap draws them on the right button or link whatever the screen size of the visitor. Desktop and mobile clicks on the same button now line up
  • New: heatmap dots follow sticky headers and other fixed elements while you scroll the preview
  • Fix: the average scroll depth on the Page Analysis page showed 0 since 1.0.4
  • Fix: deprecation notices from the CSV export on PHP 8.4 and newer
  • Export: new columns for the element path and the position inside the element
  • Clicks recorded before this version keep using page percentages

1.0.6

  • Fix (WooCommerce): the WooCommerce section was never shown on the dashboard
  • Fix (WooCommerce): clicks on the text inside add-to-cart and checkout buttons were not counted; block-based cart and checkout buttons are now recognised
  • Fix (WooCommerce): product pages are recognised by post type, so translated permalink bases work
  • Fix: a click on the text or icon inside any button or link is now attributed to that button or link
  • Privacy: GDPR mode now decides in the visitor’s browser, so it works with page caching. Nothing is stored or sent before consent. Adds support for the WP Consent API and Cookiebot, plus a heatlens_consent event for custom banners
  • Privacy: element text is only recorded for links, buttons, form labels and headings
  • Removed an unused WooCommerce script

1.0.5

  • Fix: on sites using WP Rocket’s file optimisation (or Autoptimize), visitors kept receiving an old copy of the tracking script after an update. The minified script cache is now cleared together with the page cache, so the 1.0.4 performance improvements actually reach visitors

1.0.4

  • Performance: far fewer requests to your server — events are sent at most every 15 seconds instead of every 5
  • Performance: hover tracking is now off by default (it made up about three quarters of all recorded events). Turn it on under Settings → Analysis; when on, only links and buttons are recorded
  • Performance: each batch is written with a single database query, and the rate limiter keeps one small record per IP
  • Fix: the exit scroll depth is recorded once per page view instead of on every tab switch
  • Fix: “All Clicks” on the heatmap no longer includes hover and scroll events
  • New: a cap of 300 events per page view protects busy pages

1.0.3

  • New: after a plugin update the database tables, default settings and scheduled tasks are checked automatically and page caches are cleared
  • Fix: a duplicated word in the heading of the privacy data export and the privacy policy text
  • Change: the suggested privacy policy text now mentions that the visible label of clicked buttons and links is recorded
  • Fix: demo scroll events no longer carry element details
  • Removed the bundled Turkish .po file — translations are delivered through WordPress.org language packs

1.0.2

  • Fix: heatmap preview on themes with full-screen (vh-based) sections — the preview now keeps a normal window-sized viewport and scrolls in sync with the heat layer
  • Fix: the heatmap preview now runs the page’s scripts, so sliders and lazy-loaded content look the way visitors see them
  • New: page caches (WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, WP Fastest Cache, SiteGround, Cache Enabler, Breeze, Hummingbird) are cleared automatically on activation, deactivation and when a tracking setting changes, so tracking starts right away
  • Fix: admin notices from other plugins no longer appear inside the welcome banner
  • Removed an unused nonce from the tracker configuration

1.0.1

  • New: built-in XLSX export — no external libraries needed
  • New: heatmap preview now shows the full page, so clicks below the fold are drawn in the right place
  • Fix: the suggestion engine could never find eligible pages
  • Fix: WooCommerce add-to-cart analysis query
  • Fix: rage clicks were missed after a click elsewhere; taps on mobile were counted twice
  • Fix: tracking now stops immediately when a visitor withdraws consent
  • Fix: one problem area produced several near-identical suggestions; dismissed suggestions no longer come back
  • Fix: events were not sent while the page was in the background
  • Fix: rate limit counted each request twice
  • Security: exports are downloaded through an authenticated link and deleted afterwards; spreadsheet formulas in exported data are neutralised
  • Security: the events endpoint respects the tracking setting, validates input types and no longer trusts client-supplied IP headers
  • Change: demo data is only generated on request and can be removed without touching real data
  • Change: form values and the text of large page sections are no longer recorded
  • Removed two settings that had no effect (Elementor / Gutenberg names)

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Click and touch tracking with event delegation
  • Canvas-based heatmap visualization with density threshold control
  • Smart suggestion engine with 5 analysis algorithms
  • Scroll depth tracking with IntersectionObserver
  • Rage click and dead click detection (MutationObserver)
  • Hover duration tracking (300ms+ threshold)
  • WooCommerce integration (add-to-cart, checkout, wishlist)
  • CSV, XLSX, and PDF (TCPDF) export
  • Privacy features for GDPR/KVKK (no IP, no cookies, consent plugins, Privacy Tools)
  • Admin dashboard with Chart.js graphs and weekly summary notices
  • Comparison mode for side-by-side period analysis
  • Cron-based automatic analysis (every 6 hours) and data cleanup
  • Bot filtering and rate limiting (60 req/min)
  • Welcome page with demo data generator

upgrade_notice.1.1.0: More accurate heatmaps: clicks are now positioned on the element that was clicked. The database is updated automatically.
upgrade_notice.1.0.6: Recommended for WooCommerce stores and for sites using GDPR mode together with page caching.
upgrade_notice.1.0.5: Important if you use WP Rocket or Autoptimize: makes sure visitors get the current tracking script after updates.
upgrade_notice.1.0.4: Recommended: cuts the number of tracking requests to your server by roughly two thirds. Hover tracking becomes opt-in.
upgrade_notice.1.0.3: Maintenance release: automatic upgrade checks and cache clearing after updates, plus small text fixes.
upgrade_notice.1.0.2: Fixes the heatmap preview on themes with full-screen sections and makes tracking start immediately on sites with page caching.
upgrade_notice.1.0.1: Recommended update: fixes the suggestion engine, heatmap positions below the fold and several tracking issues, and hardens exports.
